title: openai-v1: gentle deprecation shim + streaming/tool-call structured response fallback
author: Sofia Ramirez
description: Motivation: customers relying on the /v1/chat.completions semantics reported two classes of regressions after stricter param normalization: (1) streaming sessions that assumed legacy stop/role behaviors would produce truncated frames or fail to surface function toolcall handoffs, and (2) integrations that relied on legacy parameter names (e.g. stop_words, role_hint) started silently dropping fields. This PR introduces a non-breaking 'gentle deprecation' layer in the OpenAI compatibility middleware to map legacy parameters and role aliases to the canonical internal representation, plus a small runtime change to ensure the streaming coordinator emits a structured fallback envelope when a tool/function call boundary is detected but the client cannot accept the preferred framed JSON toolcall. What changed (high level): - compatibility/param_shim: add backwards-compatible mappings for legacy params (stop_words -> stop, role_hint -> role), with telemetry and warning header injected in responses so downstream integrators can detect usage. The mapping is opt-out via a compat header. - runtime/stream/coordinator: when stream handoff to a tool is required but the active client capability negotiation indicates 'framed-json' is unsupported, coordinator now emits a stable 'structured-fallback' envelope that contains: last_delta_tokens, truncated_stop_reason, and a serialized toolcall summary. This preserves functioncall semantics for older clients and reduces silent message loss. - api/openai_v1/normalizer: normalize stop arrays vs string stops, surface logprob field consistently under choices[*].logprobs.normalized for both streaming and non-streaming paths. - sdk/python/openai_compat.py and sdk/ts/client_adapter.ts: add explicit opt-in flag openai_compat_warns to surface deprecation warnings to application logs (default true in SDKs). - docs: migration guide describing the new header, how to opt-out, and examples for both framed and fallback envelopes. Commits (summary): - 7b2f4c1 add param shim + telemetry header - 2d9e7a8 streaming coordinator: structured fallback envelope - a8c3b21 normalize logprobs path across streaming/non-streaming - 145f9ab sdk: expose openai_compat_warns toggle and tests - c3179ef docs: migration guide + example curl sequences Changed files (representative): ["compat/param_shim.go", "runtime/stream/coordinator.go", "api/openai_v1/normalizer.go", "sdk/python/openai_compat.py", "sdk/typescript/client_adapter.ts", "docs/openai-v1-migration.md", "tests/integration/openai_compat_streaming.test.js", "tests/unit/param_shim_test.go", "ci/flow.yml"] Testing and CI: initial CI run failed on an edge unit test around role alias mapping (tests/unit/param_shim_test.go) due to an overlooked empty-role case; fixed in commit a8c3b21 and CI was manually retriggered. Integration tests for streaming + toolcall were added and exercised against a local framed-json-capable client and a legacy client that only accepts line-delimited JSON. Performance: added a microbenchmark for stream coordinator path to ensure fallback envelope does not add >1ms median latency per handoff at 99th percentile under our standard load; results showed ~0.6ms delta and are checked into perf/benchmarks/stream_fallback.md Rollout and risk: - This change is additive and guarded by the compat header toggles; no change in default model semantics for canonical API consumers. - We intentionally emit a deprecation warning header and SDK-level logs to encourage migration; the default shim remains enabled for six months before we will consider flipping to a stricter mode (ENG-1422). - Backwards-incompatible risk is low but possible for clients that parse streaming frames by byte offsets; we include docs and a migration snippet to detect the header and switch to framed-json when available. Review thread (high-level): - Aisha: flagged concern about header key naming and potential header bloat; suggested standardizing under x-redwood-compat and adding a short TTL to warnings. Author response: implemented x-redwood-compat-deprecation in 2d9e7a8 and added TTL logic. - Marco: requested clearer schema for structured-fallback envelope and example for Python SDK; added envelope schema to docs and sample snippet in sdk/python/openai_compat.py. - Dmitri: asked for perf numbers and a reproducible benchmark; author added microbenchmark and perf notes. Merge notes: approved by reviewers on 2025-11-21, CI green on re-run, merged via squash on 2025-11-22. Related work: follow-up ticket ENG-1499 to track removal plan and ENG-1500 to add server-side telemetry that surfaces top legacy params by customer.
review_thread_summary: Reviewer comments requested header standardization, clearer envelope schema, and perf measurements. Author implemented changes and added microbenchmarks; reviewers approved after updates.
release_notes: Added a backwards-compatible parameter shim for OpenAI /v1/chat.completions, streaming coordinator now emits a structured fallback envelope for legacy clients during tool/function handoffs, SDKs expose an opt-in deprecation warning toggle; documented migration steps.
